bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet; ROCE-focused (>40% FY26); Reinvesting in capacity aligned with firm orders; No dividends mentioned in call, focus on growth capex.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Copper price volatility (though pass-through exists); Delayed OEM model launches impacting greenfield utilization (specifically Pune); Execution risk on ramping new capacities; Currency fluctuations (JPY appreciation noted).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term growth and order book quality; Transparent about transient margin headwinds; Firm on capex discipline (only with firm orders); Slightly defensive on disclosing specific customer program details due to confidentiality.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Greenfield plants are already generating ~INR 440 Cr/quarter (near 90% of targeted INR 2,000 Cr annual run-rate) yet still loss-making due to fixed cost absorption issues from delayed volume ramp-ups at specific sites (Pune) and upfront manpower loading. The 'denominator effect' means even with full pass-through, EBITDA margins may structurally dip slightly if revenue grows purely on commodity price inflation.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The balance sheet has swung from net cash to modest net debt: External Debt of INR 9 cr / 10 cr / 61 cr and Net Debt of INR (5) cr / (56) cr / 40 cr at 31st March 2025, 31st March 2026 and 30th June 2026 respectively (figures in INR Crores).
- Including Ind AS 116 lease liabilities, Total Net Debt was INR 254 cr at 31st March 2025, INR 167 cr at 31st March 2026 and INR 239 cr at 30th June 2026; lease liabilities themselves declined steadily from INR 259 cr to INR 223 cr to INR 199 cr.
- The 31st March 2025 net cash position is stated to be "Post dividend payout of INR 575 crores (INR 354 Crores for FY 2023-24 and INR 221 Crores as interim dividend for FY 2024-25)", indicating a high-payout, asset-light capital return posture.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Joint venture entity between SAMIL and Sumitomo Wiring Systems Limited, Japan, with access to technical assistance and knowhow from Sumitomo Wiring Systems in relation to the manufacture and sale of domestic wiring harness
- Pass-through arrangement for copper as well as foreign exchange with most of its customers, so the Company does not undertake direct commodity price or foreign exchange hedging
- Debt-free status maintained through consistent financial prudence
- Credit ratings reaffirmed by CRISIL at AA+/Stable (long term) and A1+ (short term), with IND A1+ assigned by India Ratings & Research on working capital limits
- Supplies to India's top selling passenger vehicles, EV-PVs and EV 2W models
- Access to functional and management support services from SAMIL covering design and development, engineering, procurement, logistics, IT and infrastructure
- Recognised as 'One of the top 60 Sustainable Companies of India'
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate and environmental transition & physical risk — BRSR flags climate change as posing acute physical risks including extreme weather events (floods, heat stress), asset damage and increased insurance premiums, with operations in water-stressed geographies creating water-availability risk; transition risks arise from evolving regulations, stakeholder expectations and the shift to a low-carbon economy. Financial implication cited is increased operating costs from energy transition, carbon compliance, climate adaptation and supply chain disruptions, plus potential loss of business if customer sustainability expectations are not met.
- Failure to keep pace with environmental innovation and technology — Technological innovation in materials and processes is described as critical; failure to keep pace with the evolving regulatory and market landscape may impact competitiveness and stakeholder expectations, with short-term increases in capital expenditure and R&D costs and financial impact if innovation lags market expectations.
- Product sustainability and stewardship — customer expectation risk — Rising demand for low-carbon, sustainable, high-performance products aligned with electrification; the Company flags the risk of losing customers or market share and loss of competitiveness if those expectations are not met.
- Talent management, diversity, equity and inclusion — Talent attraction, retention and development are described as critical for growth, and failure in talent management can impact performance, with productivity loss due to disengagement cited as the risk.
- Human rights across operations and the value chain — Growing global scrutiny on human rights practices creates risks of violations across operations and the supplier network, with potential legal non-compliance, business interruption and reputational loss.
- Single-activity and single-industry concentration — BRSR reports 100% of turnover from the manufacture of motor vehicle electrical equipment (wiring harness & components) sold to automotive OEMs, so the Company's fortunes are tied entirely to one product line and to automotive OEM demand.
- Domestic geographic concentration with negligible exports — The Company focuses on domestic business and exports are negligible as a percentage of total turnover, leaving results dependent on the Indian automotive market with no export diversification.
- Commodity (copper) and foreign exchange exposure managed through customer pass-through — The Company states it has a pass-through arrangement for copper as well as foreign exchange for most of its customers and hence does not undertake direct commodity price or foreign exchange risk hedging — leaving residual exposure for customers not covered by the pass-through arrangement.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- The company frames itself around customer intimacy — the key-highlights slide is titled "Proud to be part of our customers' success."
- Growth is positioned as materially ahead of the end market: "Robust revenue growth of 37 % YoY, significantly outperforming industry growth", against an "Indian passenger vehicle industry grew 17% Y-o-Y in Q1FY27".
- Its fortunes are explicitly tied to the Indian PV cycle and to commodity/FX reference rates (copper, USD, Euro, Japanese Yen), which the deck discloses as standing reference tables.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: The Company was incorporated on July 02, 2020 on account of a demerger in which the domestic wiring harness business of Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL) was transferred to it, and it is engaged primarily in the manufacture and sale of wiring harness and its components to automotive original equipment manufacturers. Its BRSR disclosure classifies 100% of turnover under 'Manufacture of motor vehicle electrical equipment (Wiring Harness & Components)'. Customers primarily comprise leading automotive OEMs engaged in the design, development, manufacture, assembly, marketing and sale of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, two-wheelers, electric vehicles and related mobility solutions, which procure components from Tier-1 suppliers including the Company for integration into their vehicle manufacturing processes.
business.title: What they do

business.body: - **Wiring Harness & Components:** Wiring harness, Wiring harness components, Motor vehicle electrical equipment
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Sumitomo Wiring Systems Limited — related party: Promoter and joint venture partner. Counterparty for purchase of goods and wiring harness components including wire, metal tape, child parts, moulds, equipment & machines and capital spares/tools/jigs/fixtures; sale of wiring harness and its components and services; provision of technical assistance and knowhow for the manufacture and sale of domestic wiring harness; and support services covering engineering, design and development and software. Arrangements are ongoing and on an arm's length basis in the ordinary course of business.
- Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL) — related party: Promoter and joint venture partner; the Company was incorporated on July 02, 2020 on account of the demerger under which SAMIL's domestic wiring harness business was transferred to it. Counterparty for purchase of wiring harness components, sale of wiring harness and other parts/components/raw material/services and capital items, lease/sub-lease/licence of properties and land for manufacturing units and offices, functional support services (design and development, engineering, finance, procurement, logistics, human resource, tax and legal, IT, travel management, infrastructure) and management services. Arrangements are ongoing and on an arm's length basis in the ordinary course of business.
business.title: Group structure (profile)

business.body:
- Joint venture entity between SAMIL and Sumitomo Wiring Systems Limited, Japan, with access to technical assistance and knowhow from Sumitomo Wiring Systems in relation to the manufacture and sale of domestic wiring harness
- Pass-through arrangement for copper as well as foreign exchange with most of its customers, so the Company does not undertake direct commodity price or foreign exchange hedging
- Debt-free status maintained through consistent financial prudence
- Credit ratings reaffirmed by CRISIL at AA+/Stable (long term) and A1+ (short term), with IND A1+ assigned by India Ratings & Research on working capital limits
- Supplies to India's top selling passenger vehicles, EV-PVs and EV 2W models
- Access to functional and management support services from SAMIL covering design and development, engineering, procurement, logistics, IT and infrastructure

business.title: Competitive strengths

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin compressed by ~2.9% QoQ. Copper constitutes 24-28% of COGS; 18% sequential price rise caused ~2-2.5% bottom-line impact in Q4 due to 3-6 month pass-through lag. Polymer/PVC costs also rising but smaller impact. Manpower costs surged ~25% due to greenfield hiring, expected to normalize relative to sales.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: High teens to 20%+ expected in FY27 driven by volume; Margin: Expected to normalize to historical levels (11-12%) once greenfields stabilize and copper lag clears; Order Inflow: Strong across ICE, EV, Hybrid; Capex: ~INR 200 Cr for FY27 (mix of greenfield, brownfield, automation).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion plans strictly backed by firm customer orders; 9 out of top 10 PV OEMs are clients; No specific aggregate value disclosed, but capacity utilization targeting 80% triggers expansion.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New OEM expansions (e.g., Toyota, PMG in Aurangabad); Diversification into 2-wheelers and commercial vehicles; Automation/digitization improving productivity; Potential to redirect ICE capacity to EV if needed.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Remain deliberately powertrain-agnostic — not predicting which technology prevails, but staying relevant and ready across internal combustion, electric and hybrid platforms
- Build capability in high-voltage wiring solutions while maintaining leadership in the core low-voltage business
- Progress Greenfield ramp-ups at Navagam (Gujarat), Kharkhoda (Haryana) and Pune in line with customer programme schedules
- Deepen localisation — local design, testing and manufacturing, including in areas that were earlier more import dependent — treated as a deliberate business de-risking strategy that reduces import reliance and strengthens supply chain resilience
- Customer-led expansion: invest wherever customers need the Company, keeping facilities closely aligned with customers' own facilities and maintaining proximity and responsiveness
- Vertical integration — building many key components in house to improve responsiveness, control quality more tightly and in some cases scale faster than the industry
- Deliver solutions that are increasingly engineered in India, built in India and made for India
- Grow with discipline — invest in a measured manner only where there is clear customer visibility and long-term value, maintaining a debt-free balance sheet funded by internal cash flows
- Strengthen leadership pipelines and capability building through training, skilling, digital tools and a culture of continuous improvement
- Build on the Motherson Group's Vision 2030 journey as the Company prepares for the next phase of growth
- The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy, adopted by the Board on January 28, 2022 under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, defines the parameters for declaring or recommending a dividend while balancing the Company's need to utilise retained earnings for growth and sustainability. Subject to the Companies Act, SEBI Listing Regulations, the articles of association and prevailing financial or market conditions, the Board will adhere to the policy for 'distribution of up to 40% of profit' as dividend, and may decide a higher dividend in special and exceptional circumstances. The policy sets out broad criteria for determining the proposed dividend so as to appropriately reward shareholders while supporting the future growth of the Company.
- Implementation of a comprehensive decarbonisation roadmap aligned with strategic ambitions and targets
- Increased use of renewable energy
- Reduction in resource consumption, emissions, waste and water usage
- Water stewardship initiatives in high-risk (water-stressed) locations
- Implementation of long-term climate transition and innovation strategies, with development of recyclable, reusable and resource-efficient materials and a focus on reducing, reusing and recycling waste streams
- Collaboration with suppliers and customers to improve environmental performance and enable circular-economy solutions
- Integration of sustainability into product design and development, with assessment and reduction of product carbon footprint
- Alignment with the UN Global Compact, deployment of a Human Rights policy, assessment using third-party tools and integration of human rights into supply chain processes
- Diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives and policies, leadership development and capability building, employee engagement and well-being/mental-health programmes
- Independent reasonable assurance obtained on BRSR Core disclosures (assurance provider S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP), voluntarily extended to selected non-Core BRSR KPIs to enhance transparency
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Driven by growing customer demand, MSWIL continued through FY2025-26 to invest in ramp-up activities progressing across its Greenfield locations at Navagam in Gujarat, Kharkhoda in Haryana and Pune, with the Board's Report listing 'operational ramp-up across greenfield locations' as a key highlight of the year. Management describes these as long-term investments essential to maintaining proximity to customers, enhancing responsiveness and supporting sustained growth on a stronger operational foundation, and notes that while customer launch timelines and volume schedules may shift from time to time, the underlying direction remains unchanged. The Chairman states the Company will continue to invest in growth but always in a measured manner, with clear visibility and prudent use of capital, funded without debt. No capex amount, capacity figure or commissioning date is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Vehicles are becoming more feature-rich and electronically sophisticated, and premiumisation is steadily shaping demand, making wiring systems increasingly critical to vehicle performance, safety and complexity
- Higher wiring harness content per vehicle, combined with the nature of the platforms supported, driving growth ahead of the broader industry
- New OEM programme launches, with the Company present on several new programmes, sustaining growth momentum
- Industry passenger-vehicle volumes grew modestly while the Company recorded healthy growth across quarters
- The market is progressing across internal combustion, electric and hybrid platforms — an evolving mix rather than one technology replacing another overnight
- Deep customer trust translating into more platforms, higher content and greater responsibility entrusted to the Company
- Copper prices remained elevated, with effective pass-through mechanisms supporting cost management
- Underlying profitability remained stable excluding Greenfields, while the Company continued to operate without debt
- MSWIL serves both long-standing customers and emerging new-age clients, and is described as future-ready and aligned with customer expansion plans
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: MSWIL crossed INR 10,000 Cr annual revenue with 33% YoY growth in Q4, driven by volume gains and copper price pass-through, though margins faced transient compression due to commodity lag and greenfield start-up costs. Profitability is expected to normalize in FY27 as new plants reach 80% utilization and copper prices stabilize.

open.item: The Directors recommended for members' approval a dividend of Re. 0.58 per equity share of face value Re. 1 each for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, with a record date of July 14, 2026.
The Board will adhere to the Dividend Distribution Policy for distribution of up to 40% of profit as dividend, balancing shareholder returns with retained earnings for growth.

Under the shareholder-approved 'Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited - Employee Stock Option Scheme 2025', up to 1,55,00,000 employee stock options will be granted to eligible employees, exercisable into up to 1,55,00,000 equity shares of face value Re. 1 each, administered through the MSWIL ESOP Trust.
The Company will continue to progress Greenfield ramp-ups at Navagam, Kharkhoda and Pune in line with customer programme schedules.
The Company remains committed to strengthening localisation and delivering solutions that are increasingly engineered in India, built in India and made for India.

The Company will expand capabilities across evolving vehicle architectures and powertrain technologies, strengthening high-voltage wiring harness solutions while maintaining leadership in the core low-voltage business.

The Company will continue to invest in growth in a measured manner with clear visibility and prudent use of capital, maintaining its debt-free balance sheet so internal cash flows fund investment for customers.
MSWIL will continue ramp-up activities at its Greenfield facilities in Navagam (Gujarat), Kharkhoda (Haryana) and Pune, in line with customer launch timelines.
The Company will continue to invest in growth in a measured manner, only where there is clear visibility, with prudent use of capital.

risks.risk: Climate and environmental transition & physical risk
risks.note: BRSR flags climate change as posing acute physical risks including extreme weather events (floods, heat stress), asset damage and increased insurance premiums, with operations in water-stressed geographies creating water-availability risk; transition risks arise from evolving regulations, stakeholder expectations and the shift to a low-carbon economy. Financial implication cited is increased operating costs from energy transition, carbon compliance, climate adaptation and supply chain disruptions, plus potential loss of business if customer sustainability expectations are not met.

risks.risk: Failure to keep pace with environmental innovation and technology
risks.note: Technological innovation in materials and processes is described as critical; failure to keep pace with the evolving regulatory and market landscape may impact competitiveness and stakeholder expectations, with short-term increases in capital expenditure and R&D costs and financial impact if innovation lags market expectations.

risks.risk: Product sustainability and stewardship — customer expectation risk
risks.note: Rising demand for low-carbon, sustainable, high-performance products aligned with electrification; the Company flags the risk of losing customers or market share and loss of competitiveness if those expectations are not met.

risks.risk: Talent management, diversity, equity and inclusion
risks.note: Talent attraction, retention and development are described as critical for growth, and failure in talent management can impact performance, with productivity loss due to disengagement cited as the risk.

risks.risk: Human rights across operations and the value chain
risks.note: Growing global scrutiny on human rights practices creates risks of violations across operations and the supplier network, with potential legal non-compliance, business interruption and reputational loss.

BRSR reports 100% of turnover from the manufacture of motor vehicle electrical equipment (wiring harness & components) sold to automotive OEMs, so the Company's fortunes are tied entirely to one product line and to automotive OEM demand.

risks.risk: Domestic geographic concentration with negligible exports
risks.note: The Company focuses on domestic business and exports are negligible as a percentage of total turnover, leaving results dependent on the Indian automotive market with no export diversification.

risks.risk: Commodity (copper) and foreign exchange exposure managed through customer pass-through
risks.note: The Company states it has a pass-through arrangement for copper as well as foreign exchange for most of its customers and hence does not undertake direct commodity price or foreign exchange risk hedging — leaving residual exposure for customers not covered by the pass-through arrangement.

one-line thesis: MSWIL crossed INR 10,000 Cr annual revenue with 33% YoY growth in Q4, driven by volume gains and copper price pass-through, though margins faced transient compression due to commodity lag and greenfield start-up costs. Profitability is expected to normalize in FY27 as new plants reach 80% utilization and copper prices stabilize.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,850 Cr (Q4, +33% YoY), Full Year >INR 10,000 Cr; EBITDA Margin: Compressed ~290 bps QoQ to ~9-10% range due to copper lag & start-up costs; PAT: Impacted by INR 127 Cr full-year greenfield start-up costs; Order Book: Robust, expansion backed by firm OEM orders; Net Debt: Zero (Debt-free since inception). One-offs: INR 127 Cr greenfield start-up costs (FY26), Copper price lag impact (~2-2.5% bottom line effect in Q4).
guidance: Revenue Growth: High teens to 20%+ expected in FY27 driven by volume; Margin: Expected to normalize to historical levels (11-12%) once greenfields stabilize and copper lag clears; Order Inflow: Strong across ICE, EV, Hybrid; Capex: ~INR 200 Cr for FY27 (mix of greenfield, brownfield, automation).
order book & pipeline: Expansion plans strictly backed by firm customer orders; 9 out of top 10 PV OEMs are clients; No specific aggregate value disclosed, but capacity utilization targeting 80% triggers expansion.
segment / subsidiary detail: Greenfield plants (Kharkhoda ~80% util, Navagam ~60% util, Pune ~40-50% util) contributed ~INR 440 Cr in Q4 (annualized run-rate ~INR 2,000 Cr). Pune lagging due to delayed model launches. ICE, EV, and Hybrid segments all seeing order wins.
growth verticals / optionality: New OEM expansions (e.g., Toyota, PMG in Aurangabad); Diversification into 2-wheelers and commercial vehicles; Automation/digitization improving productivity; Potential to redirect ICE capacity to EV if needed.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin compressed by ~2.9% QoQ. Copper constitutes 24-28% of COGS; 18% sequential price rise caused ~2-2.5% bottom-line impact in Q4 due to 3-6 month pass-through lag. Polymer/PVC costs also rising but smaller impact. Manpower costs surged ~25% due to greenfield hiring, expected to normalize relative to sales.
capex / expansion: FY26: ~INR 190 Cr; FY27 Guidance: ~INR 200 Cr. Mix includes greenfield completion, brownfield expansion, automation, and replacement capex.
capital allocation: Debt-free balance sheet; ROCE-focused (>40% FY26); Reinvesting in capacity aligned with firm orders; No dividends mentioned in call, focus on growth capex.
risks & watch-items: Copper price volatility (though pass-through exists); Delayed OEM model launches impacting greenfield utilization (specifically Pune); Execution risk on ramping new capacities; Currency fluctuations (JPY appreciation noted).
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term growth and order book quality; Transparent about transient margin headwinds; Firm on capex discipline (only with firm orders); Slightly defensive on disclosing specific customer program details due to confidentiality.

The 'denominator effect' means even with full pass-through, EBITDA margins may structurally dip slightly if revenue grows purely on commodity price inflation.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company was incorporated on July 02, 2020 on account of a demerger in which the domestic wiring harness business of Samvardhana Motherson International Limited (SAMIL) was transferred to it, and it is engaged primarily in the manufacture and sale of wiring harness and its components to automotive original equipment manufacturers. Its BRSR disclosure classifies 100% of turnover under 'Manufacture of motor vehicle electrical equipment (Wiring Harness & Components)'. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Vehicles are becoming more feature-rich and electronically sophisticated, and premiumisation is steadily shaping demand, making wiring systems increasingly critical to vehicle performance, safety and complexity
- Higher wiring harness content per vehicle, combined with the nature of the platforms supported, driving growth ahead of the broader industry
- New OEM programme launches, with the Company present on several new programmes, sustaining growth momentum
- Industry passenger-vehicle volumes grew modestly while the Company recorded healthy growth across quarters
- The market is progressing across internal combustion, electric and hybrid platforms — an evolving mix rather than one technology replacing another overnight
- Deep customer trust translating into more platforms, higher content and greater responsibility entrusted to the Company
- Copper prices remained elevated, with effective pass-through mechanisms supporting cost management
- Underlying profitability remained stable excluding Greenfields, while the Company continued to operate without debt
- MSWIL serves both long-standing customers and emerging new-age clients, and is described as future-ready and aligned with customer expansion plans

Polymer/PVC costs also rising but smaller impact. Manpower costs surged ~25% due to greenfield hiring, expected to normalize relative to sales.

capex_expansion.body: Driven by growing customer demand, MSWIL continued through FY2025-26 to invest in ramp-up activities progressing across its Greenfield locations at Navagam in Gujarat, Kharkhoda in Haryana and Pune, with the Board's Report listing 'operational ramp-up across greenfield locations' as a key highlight of the year. Management describes these as long-term investments essential to maintaining proximity to customers, enhancing responsiveness and supporting sustained growth on a stronger operational foundation, and notes that while customer launch timelines and volume schedules may shift from time to time, the underlying direction remains unchanged. themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
